solution: Many young members of Annie Besant's Home Rule League also participated in the Satyagraha meeting.

question: Where did Gandhiji establish his first ashram after returning to India?
solution: Sabarmati Ashram became the main center of Gandhiji's activities. It was from here that he planned the Dandi March and many important movements.

question: When did Gandhiji use 'Satyagraha' for the first time in South Africa?
solution: Satyagraha means 'insistence for truth'. According to Gandhiji, this is not a weapon of the weak but the use of spiritual strength.

question: Which leader's death during the 'Non-Cooperation Movement' had left the entire country in mourning?
solution: After Tilak's death, Gandhiji shouldered the bier and 'Tilak Swaraj Fund' was created in his memory, which was very successful.

question: Which was the most successful boycott of foreign goods during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
solution: The burning of foreign clothes became the most visible and influential part of the movement.

question: Who called the withdrawal of non-cooperation movement as “National Calamity”?
solution: Due to this disappointment, a new faction (Swaraj Party) emerged within the Congress which wanted to adopt a different path from Gandhiji's strategy.

question: Who founded 'Rowlat Satyagraha Sabha' to oppose the Rowlatt Act?
solution: Rowlatt Satyagraha was the first nationwide political movement launched by Gandhiji in India. During this movement, huge tension had arisen in Punjab.

question: In which year was 'Tolstoy Farm' established near Johannesburg?
solution: Tolstoy Farm was the center of residence and training of Satyagrahis. Gandhiji was deeply influenced by Leo Tolstoy's philosophy of 'non-violence' and 'the Kingdom of God is within you'.

question: Which law was passed as a result of Champaran Satyagraha?
solution: चंपारण सत्याग्रह में राजेंद्र प्रसाद, मजहर-उल-हक और जे.बी. Leaders like Kripalani also supported Gandhiji. This was Gandhiji's first major victory in India.

question: खेड़ा सत्याग्रह के दौरान इंदुलाल याज्ञिक की क्या भूमिका थी?
solution: खेड़ा आंदोलन ने कई युवा नेताओं को तैयार किया जिन्होंने बाद में भारत के स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई।

question: Which law did Gandhiji call 'black law'?
solution: रौलट एक्ट का आधिकारिक नाम 'अनार्किकल एंड रिवोल्यूशनरी क्राइम्स एक्ट' था। इसके विरोध में गांधीजी ने 'रौलट सत्याग्रह' शुरू किया और 'ना कोई वकील, ना कोई अपील, ना कोई दलील' का नारा प्रसिद्ध हुआ।

question: Why was Gandhiji given the title of 'Kaiser-e-Hind'?
options: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के अध्यक्ष बनने पर
बोअर युद्ध में उनकी सेवाओं के लिए
solution: गांधीजी ने जलियांवाला बाग हत्याकांड और ब्रिटिश सरकार के अन्यायपूर्ण व्यवहार के विरोध में 1920 में यह उपाधि वापस कर दी थी।

question: C.R. In which year did Das die, which dealt a major blow to the Swaraj Party?
solution: C.R. On Das's death, Gandhiji had said that he had lost a great companion and the country had lost a true patriot.

question: How many policemen were killed in the Chauri-Chaura incident?
solution: This violence made Gandhiji realize that the people of India were not yet completely ready for non-violent movement.

question: Where in India did Gandhiji's first public appearance take place?
solution: BHU was founded by Madan Mohan Malviya. In his speech, Gandhiji criticized the Indian elite and stressed on connecting with the masses.

question: Which Indian leader refused or returned the title of 'Knighthood' during the Non-Cooperation Movement? (PDF Note: Comparison with reference to Tagore)
solution: This sacrifice of Tagore caused disrepute to the British government at the international level.

question: How many times did Mahatma Gandhi preside over the Congress in his life?
solution: Gandhiji preferred to work as an ordinary member or guide rather than the post of president, so that he could rise above the organization and serve the public.

question: Which were the two houses of the 'Bicameral Legislature' established at the Center under the Act of 1919?
options: House of Lords and House of Commons
solution: The number of elected members in the Central Assembly was increased, but real power still rested with the Viceroy.

question: What is the meaning of 'Tin' and 'Kathiya' in the word 'Tinkathiya'?
solution: This exploitative practice was abolished by the Champaran Agricultural Act in 1918 after the Champaran Satyagraha.

question: Why were the leaders of Swaraj Party called 'transformationists'?
options: They wanted a change in the old policy of boycott
They wanted to convert the British
They wanted to change the name of India
solution: The 'reformists' believed that leaving the councils vacant was tantamount to allowing the British to rule without opposition.

question: Who presided over the 'Gaya Conference' (1922)?
solution: The Gaya session was an important turning point in the history of the Congress where there was a direct confrontation between the 'changeist' and 'conservative' factions.

question: What is the distance from 'Kocharab Ashram' to 'Sabarmati Ashram'? (PDF Note: With reference to Ahmedabad)
solution: Kochrab Ashram was Gandhiji's first home in India, but Sabarmati became his longest working place.

question: What did the Congress' 'Madan Mohan Malviya Committee' report say on the number of people killed in Jallianwala Bagh?
options: No one died in the incident
All the people were British citizens.
The death toll was more than 1000.
solution: Motilal Nehru and Gandhiji were also members of this investigation committee of Congress. This report exposed the inhuman face of the British to the public.

question: What does 'Tinkathia System' mean?
options: Growing indigo on 3 katha of land per bigha
solution: Cultivation of indigo reduced the fertility of the land and after the introduction of chemical dyes, farmers were incurring huge losses, yet the landlords were pressurizing them.

question: When did the 'Prince of Wales' arrive in India during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
solution: There were terrible riots when the Prince of Wales reached Bombay, due to which Gandhiji was very sad and he fasted.

question: Where did Gandhiji establish 'Natal Indian Congress' in South Africa?
solution: Through the Natal Indian Congress, Indians for the first time got organized and started submitting petitions for their problems.

question: When did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
solution: The crowd had gathered to protest the arrest of two leaders – Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal. General Dyer had ordered to open fire on the unarmed crowd without any warning.

question: Who was the main assistant of Gandhiji during the Kheda Satyagraha, who was later called the 'Iron Man'?
solution: Kheda Satyagraha gave Vallabhbhai Patel a new identity in Indian politics and from here his loyalty towards Gandhiji began.

question: Who was the woman leader who helped Gandhiji in the Ahmedabad mill strike?
solution: It was Anusuya Sarabhai who had called Gandhiji to Ahmedabad. Later he founded the Ahmedabad Textile Labor Association.

question: Who was the 'Lieutenant Governor' of Bihar at the time of Champaran Satyagraha?
solution: Edward Gate had invited Gandhiji to become a member of the inquiry committee, thereby acknowledging that the farmers' grievances were genuine.

question: Against whom did Gandhiji start his first Satyagraha in South Africa?
solution: The Satyagraha of 1906 in South Africa was the first major experiment in non-violent resistance. During this time, Gandhiji had also protested against the government not recognizing Hindu marriages.

question: Who was the 'Lieutenant Governor' of Punjab at the time of Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
solution: General Dyer was called the 'Butcher of Amritsar', while Michael O'Dwyer gave administrative approval to this entire repressive policy.
